Even if, Heaven forbid, one has fallen many, many times beyond count — nevertheless, every movement he makes to lift himself each time from his fall, and every cry he cries — even from the lowest depths — is never, ever lost. As our Rebbe said: even a cry from the lowest abyss is never lost, however things may be afterward. For Hashem and His Torah are Ein Sof — without limit. Just as there is no ceiling to ascent (for there is always higher), so too there is no floor to descent — from any fall, there could be worse. Therefore one must strengthen himself not to fall further, and the essential strength comes from the Tzaddikim described above.

For they merited to perceive that just as there is no ultimate ascent, likewise there is no descent from which one cannot rise. In truth it is all one: the more the Tzaddik ascends, the more he perceives Hashem's chassadim — which is the essential greatness of Hashem, for the attribute of Chesed is called Gedulah [greatness]: "Lecha Hashem haGedulah" — and Gedulah = Chesed. The more one perceives Hashem's greatness, the more one perceives His chassadim. Therefore, these Tzaddikim who never stand still, ascending ever higher and perceiving ever more of His greatness (His chassadim) — through this they merit to perceive that there is no fall and no despair in the world at all. For they perceive such chassadim — the essential greatness of the Creator — through which everyone can ascend.

This is what our Rebbe said in the Torah "Mishra d'Sakina" (LM I:30): one specifically needs a Tzaddik exceedingly great in stature, for the greater the illness, the greater the physician and healer needed. The greater the Tzaddik, the more he can raise up even those who have fallen very far — until through the power of the Tzaddikim described above, there is no fall and no descent from which one cannot rise by their power, if he merits to believe in them and draw close to them. All this is the aspect of Arichas Apayim: Erech Apayim for the righteous (who must extend their spirit — not letting their additional spirit and chiyus cease on account of their great ascent and lofty level, but extending their spirit to seek an even higher level and begin anew), and Erech Apayim for the wicked (even those who have fallen to complete wickedness — as long as the neshamah is within him, as long as he can still move even one limb, he must extend his patience and spirit to constantly await Hashem's salvation and to strengthen himself to begin anew in whatever way he can). For no movement of holiness, no sigh, no cry, no holy yearning is ever lost — for Hashem never casts away forever.

All this is the aspect of Tefillin, which are the aspect of Arichas Apayim — the new Mochin and life that one draws through the mitzvah of Tefillin, from the holy elders who receive from the uppermost elder, the Blind Beggar.

This is the aspect of the ma'abarta [housing/passageway] of the Tefillin through which the retzuos [straps] pass, which is the aspect of Ma'avar Yabok [the crossing of the Yabok], as brought in the Kavanos. For the retzuos are the aspect of the drawing-down of the Mochin of the Tefillin — the light of the countenance — the aspect of the Thirteen Tikkunei D'ikna, the aspect of Erech Apayim. Therefore retzuah [strap] has the numerical value of 370 — the aspect of the 370 lights of the countenance (shin-ayin nehorin). The retzuos are long — this is the aspect of Erech Apayim — extending upon oneself the lengthening of spirit.

Through this, the aspect of retzuah bisha [the evil strap] is sweetened and nullified — the strap for striking the wicked, from which all suffering and harsh judgments originate. Through the aspect of Erech Apayim drawn through the long retzuos drawn from the light of the countenance (the Tefillin-Mochin), one passes over all sufferings and sweetens them. They lose the power to nullify and prevent one from serving the Creator — for one merits Arichas Apayim: extending his spirit over everything, his spirit never shortened by any suffering or obstacle, simply doing what he must: engaging in Torah and avodah — until he merits to pass over them and nullify them. For by not looking at the obstacles at all, through Arichas Apayim, they are nullified of themselves. All suffering and obstacles come only as a test — and when one is firm in his mind and extends his spirit and pays them no attention, they are nullified of themselves before him.

Therefore the length of the retzuah — which is the drawing-down of the light of the countenance, the aspect of Arichas Apayim — nullifies the retzuah bisha from which all sufferings derive, for everything is sweetened and nullified through Arichas Apayim, which is the sweetening of judgments, the suppression of anger and din.

This is the aspect of the ma'abarta of the Tefillin through which the straps pass — the aspect of Ma'avar Yabok. Yabok has the numerical value of Havayah Elokim [= 112]. This is the aspect of "BaHashem ahaleil davar, bEilokim ahaleil davar" — "In Hashem I will praise a word, in Elokim I will praise a word" (Tehillim 56:11). One must recognize Hashem and draw close to Him always — whether in good or in trouble, in ascent or in descent: "BaHashem ahaleil... bEilokim ahaleil..." As brought in the Torah "Mi ha'ish hechafetz chayim" (LM I:33).

This is itself the aspect of being baki baHalachah [expert in the law], as brought in the Torah "Kra es Yehoshua" (LM I:6) — that whoever wishes to do teshuvah must be a "baki": baki b'ratzo [expert in running forward], baki b'shov [expert in returning], baki b'ayil [expert in entering], baki b'nafik [expert in going out] — the aspect of "Im esak Shamayim sham Atah, v'atziah She'ol hineka" — "If I ascend to Heaven — You are there; if I make my bed in the depths — behold, You are there" (Tehillim 139:8). One must always seek to draw close to Hashem wherever he is — in ascent or descent — and even if he is in the lowest abyss, from there too he can draw close to Him: "V'atziah She'ol hineka."

All this is the aspect of Arichas Apayim — to always extend one's spirit all the days of his life, however things may be, never falling from anything, always beginning to draw close to Him. Similarly, one should never weary even if he has merited a great ascent to a lofty level — he should know that even in the heavens Hashem is found ("Im esak Shamayim sham Atah") — even though it seems he has ascended to the heavens, he still needs to seek Hashem and begin anew, for Hashem is found even in the heavens. As our Rebbe said in the Torah "Ki seitzei lamilchamah" (LM II:82).

All this is merited through Tefillin — Arichas Apayim. This is the ma'abarta — the aspect of Ma'avar, the name Yabok. For Yabok is the letters baki — baki b'ratzo, baki b'shov — as our Rebbe himself said there: this baki is the aspect of Yabok. And Yabok has the numerical value of Havayah Elokim — "BaHashem ahaleil, bEilokim ahaleil" — whether with the attribute of Mercy or the attribute of Judgment, whether in good or in trouble, in ascent or in descent: one must always serve Hashem and extend his spirit, never falling, never tiring, never ceasing his yearning for Hashem — on account of nothing in the world. All this is merited through Tefillin — Arichas Apayim.

This is the aspect of the long retzuos passing through the ma'abarta — through which one passes over all sufferings, obstacles, and confusions that are drawn from the retzuah bisha. Everything is nullified before him through Arichas Apayim. This is the aspect of: "Vaya'avor Hashem al panav" — "Hashem passed over his face" (Shemos 34:6) — which is the aspect of the ma'abarta. For then, when Hashem passed over his face, He revealed the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy — the Tleissar Tikkunei D'ikna. There it says: "Vay'maher Moshe" — that he saw Erech Apayim. This is the aspect of Tefillin. Then He revealed the light of Tefillin, as written there in that parshah: "Ani a'avir kol tuvi... v'raisa es achorai" — "I shall pass all My goodness... and you shall see My back" — and our Sages expounded (Berachos 7a): "This is the knot of Tefillin." For the essential Tefillin are drawn from there — from the Tikkunei D'ikna, the Thirteen Attributes, the aspect of Erech Apayim.

The essential Arichas Apayim is merited through Eretz Yisrael, which is the aspect of emunah, as written there in the Torah cited above on the verse "Vay'maher Moshe" (LM I:155). This is the aspect of Tefillin: the parshiyos in Tefillin speak of Eretz Yisrael and emunah. The first two parshiyos primarily concern Yetzias Mitzrayim and the entry into Eretz Yisrael: "Zachor es hayom hazeh asher yetzasem miMitzrayim... v'hayah ki yevi'acha Hashem el ha'Aretz" (Shemos 13). And the second parshah begins: "V'hayah ki yevi'acha..."

For the essential Tefillin are the aspect of Arichas Apayim merited through Eretz Yisrael — the opposite of Mitzrayim, which is full of idolatry, the opposite of emunah. Therefore, when they were in Mitzrayim, it says: "V'lo sham'u el Moshe mikotzer ruach" — "They did not listen to Moshe because of kotzer ruach [shortness of spirit]" (Shemos 6:9) — they could not draw close to the Tzaddik (Moshe) and listen to him, due to kotzer ruach, the opposite of Arichas Apayim through which is the essential drawing close to Hashem and to the true Tzaddikim.

The latter two parshiyos speak of emunah: Shema Yisrael = faith in the Unity; V'hayah im shamoa = acceptance of the yoke of mitzvos and nullification of avodah zarah — which is the aspect of charon af [fierce anger], the opposite of Arichas Apayim: "Hishamru lachem... v'sartem va'avadtem elohim acheirim v'charah af" (Devarim 11:16-17).

Thus all four parshiyos of Tefillin speak of leaving Mitzrayim (= avodah zarah, charon af, kotzer ruach) to merit entering Eretz Yisrael (= emunah, Arichas Apayim) — the essential aspect of Tefillin. Therefore the final parshah concludes: "L'ma'an yirbu yemeichem vimei vneichem" — "That your days may be lengthened, and the days of your children" (Devarim 11:21) — long life merited through Tefillin = Erech Apayim, extending the spirit, from which comes long life. The essential life is through the breath of the spirit — through Arichas Ruach = Erech Apayim = the holy Zakein = long life.

Therefore our Sages said (Pesachim 113b): "HaRaschan, chayav einam chayim" — "The hot-tempered person — his life is not a life." For the hot-tempered person is the aspect of kotzer ruach, the opposite of Arichas Apayim — therefore his life is not a life. The essential life comes from Arichas HaRuach = Erech Apayim.

Therefore one must bind the Tefillin on the left arm — the aspect of yad keihah [the weaker hand], as our Sages said. For the essential Tefillin = Erech Apayim: to sweeten and nullify the aspect of yad keihah, from which all suffering and obstacles originate. One must extend his spirit through Arichas Apayim and pass over everything — not having kotzer ruach, which is the aspect of "Ruach necheiah mi yisa'enah" — "A broken spirit, who can bear it?" (Mishlei 18:14). Rather, he must extend his spirit over everything — this being Tefillin, Arichas Apayim — through which yad keihah is sweetened.

This is: "Vayomer Hashem el Avram: Lech lecha mei'artzecha umimoladtecha umibeis avicha el ha'Aretz" — "Hashem said to Avram: Go forth from your land, your birthplace, and your father's house, to the Land" (Bereishis 12:1) — to Eretz Yisrael. This is juxtaposed to the verse: "Vayamas Terach b'Charan" — "Terach died in Charan." Rashi explains: until here was the charon af [fierce anger] of the Omnipresent. Therefore, juxtaposed to this, Hashem commanded Avraham to go to Eretz Yisrael — for through this he would sweeten and nullify the charon af. Through Eretz Yisrael one merits Erech Apayim, the opposite of charon af. For Avraham is the head of the believers — therefore he was the first to whom the holiness of Eretz Yisrael was revealed, as brought in the holy Zohar: "He weighed on the scales until it was revealed to him." For Eretz Yisrael is the aspect of emunah, the aspect of Arichas Apayim.

This is the aspect of: "Kadeish li chol bechor peter kol rechem bivnei Yisrael" — "Sanctify to Me every firstborn, the first issue of every womb among the children of Yisrael" (Shemos 13:2) — which is the beginning of the first parshah of Tefillin. The essential Tefillin are drawn from the aspect of the holiness of the bechoros [firstborn] — the first birth, the aspect of Yetzias Mitzrayim, which is the aspect of birth. Because of this, one must sanctify the first birth — the bechor. All this is to draw upon oneself the holiness of the birth of the Mochin — the essential birth: to merit renewing his chiyus and brain each time as if born today — the essential long life = Tefillin.

Therefore one must give the bechor to the Kohen, or redeem him from the Kohen. The Kohen is the aspect of the holy Zakein: "Kashemen hatov al harosh yored al hazakein, z'kan Aharon" — "Like the fine oil upon the head, descending upon the beard — the beard of Aharon" (Tehillim 133:2) — the aspect of the T'manya Tikkunei D'ikna d'Chahana Rabba [eight rectifications of the beard of the High Priest]. And our Sages said (Shabbos 151b): "V'shemen al roshcha al yechsar" — "Let not oil be lacking on your head" (Koheles 9:8) — these are the Tefillin shel Rosh. For the essential Tefillin are drawn from "Kashemen hatov al harosh... z'kan Aharon."

By giving the bechor (the first birth) to the Kohen, one draws the holiness of the birth of the Mochin and chiyus — meriting to renew himself each time as if born today. This is the essential Tefillin — the Mochin and long life received from the holy Zakein who said he is exceedingly old yet has not begun to live at all, as if born today — beginning anew each time.

This is the aspect of Mashiach, of whom it says: "Ani hayom yelidticha" — "I have this day given birth to you" (Tehillim 2:7). Mashiach will merit this aspect in perfection — long life where one begins living anew each moment as if born today: "Ani hayom yelidticha." For Mashiach will attain the aspect of above time, as explained in the words of our Rebbe on this verse. The Blind Beggar's boast — exceedingly old yet yanak, the whole world not amounting to a blink of an eye — this is the aspect of above time. This is the long life Mashiach will merit: "Chayim sha'al mimcha, nasata lo" — "He asked life of You, You gave it to him" (Tehillim 21:5) — the aspect of Dovid Melech Yisrael chai v'kayam. For Dovid is Mashiach. This is the aspect of Tefillin — there is the root of Mashiach's neshamah. The root of Mashiach's kingship is in the kesher shel Tefillin [knot of Tefillin]. As our Rebbe said (LM I:54): "V'haysah nefesh adoni tzerurah bitzeror hachayim" — "The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life" (Shmuel I 25:29) — said regarding Dovid, who is Mashiach. "Tzeror HaChayim" = the kesher shel Tefillin, which is the aspect of life — long life.

This is the aspect of the retzuah of the head that descends from the knot down to the navel. The holiness of Tefillin comes from the zekeinim who merited to sanctify their brains so greatly that they remembered what happened from the beginning of their birth — when the umbilical cord was cut. The essential completion of birth — the aspect of Tefillin, "Kadeish li chol bechor peter kol rechem" — is the cutting of the umbilical cord. Therefore it says regarding Yetzias Mitzrayim (Yechezkel 16:4): "Umolodosayich b'yom huleches osach, lo karas shorereich" — "On the day of your birth, your navel cord was not cut" — before the Exodus they were like a child whose umbilical cord was not yet cut.

For although the other elders remembered even further back, nevertheless it is impossible to reveal their holiness outwardly — only the holiness of the brain of the elder who remembered the beginning of birth (cutting the umbilical cord) — the essential aspect of Tefillin, which speak of birth: "Kadeish li chol bechor." Would that we merit to receive even his holiness! The holiness of the Mochin of the other elders is not revealed outwardly at all — their light is concealed only in the parshiyos hidden inside the batim [housings]. From there, their holiness is received in a hidden and concealed manner — for the holiness of their memory is exceedingly beyond us, as the discerning will understand.

One retzuah extends down to the heart. For the retzuah is the aspect of the light drawn from Arichas Apayim. Therefore it must be drawn down to the heart — to introduce Arichas Apayim, the suppression of anger, into the heart — so that one has no hakpadah [resentment/ill-feeling] at all, not even in the heart.

This is the essential Arichas Apayim. As our Rebbe said of himself: he merited this aspect in Eretz Yisrael — that he would have such Arichas Apayim that there would not be in his heart even the slightest trace of anger or resentment, even against his greatest enemy who causes him all manner of suffering. Nevertheless, he has in his heart against that person no hatred and no resentment. This is the essential Arichas Apayim. Therefore the retzuah must be drawn to the heart — to introduce Arichas Apayim into the heart — so that nothing bothers him at all, not even in the heart.

This is the aspect of Hashem's praise for Kneses Yisrael: "Shor'rareich agan hasahar al yechsar hamezeg" — "Your navel is a round basin; let the blended wine not be lacking" (Shir HaShirim 7:3). Our Sages expounded (Sanhedrin 37a) on the seventy members of the Sanhedrin, who would sit in a semicircle like the moon. "Shor'rareich" — this is the aspect of the retzuah of Tefillin that descends from the knot of the head down to the navel, which is drawn from the aspect of the kingship of Dovid Mashiach who lives and endures — the aspect of the knot of the head. From there the strap extends down to the navel: the aspect of "Shor'rareich agan hasahar" — the seventy Sanhedrin, corresponding to the seventy faces of Torah. Dovid sits at their head, as our Sages expounded on the verse "Yosheiv basheves tachk'moni rosh" (Shmuel II 23:8).

All the seventy Sanhedrin — the seventy faces of Torah — receive from Dovid Mashiach, whose entire chiyus comes from the elders — the Tikkunei D'ikna Kadisha, the splendor of the countenance, the aspect of stories of primordial years, from which all seventy faces of Torah are drawn, as explained in the Torah "Pasach Rabbi Shimon" (LM I:60). Through them, one awakens from sheinah [sleep] — the departure of the Mochin. Through the elders and the stories of primordial years, all seventy faces of Torah are drawn and one awakens from sleep.

This is the aspect of the seventy years that Dovid HaMelech lived. Therefore he minimized sleep exceedingly, as our Sages said (Sukkah 26b): Dovid never slept more than sixty breaths — so that he should not taste the taste of death. For sleep is one-sixtieth of death, drawn through the sin of Adam HaRishon, who ate from the Eitz HaDa'as [Tree of Knowledge] and blemished the Eitz HaChayim [Tree of Life] — which is the aspect of the light of Tefillin. For Tefillin = life = the Eitz HaChayim, of which it says: "V'achal v'chai l'olam" — "And he shall eat and live forever" (Bereishis 3:22).

Had Adam not sinned, he would have merited true life — eternal life, long life while still in the body: while still in the body he could have been included in the Ein Sof forever in ratzo vashov [running and returning], living long life — renewing his chiyus forever in the aspect of the renewal of life of the uppermost elder, the Blind Beggar, who is always old and always yanak. But after sinning, eating from the Eitz HaDa'as Tov vaRa, being driven from Gan Eden, and having the contamination of the serpent (mishka d'chivya) cling to his body — now it is impossible to live in the body forever. One can only merit eternal life through death, which is a great good: "V'hinei tov me'od — zeh hamaves" — "Behold, it is very good — this is death" (Bereishis Rabbah 9). Through death (= sleep), the brain is renewed, the body is purified, and at the resurrection one will rise in a pure body completely cleansed of the serpent's contamination. Then one will merit to receive new Mochin — the aspect of Tefillin, the Eitz HaChayim — long life: life that is added each moment, where the more one ages the more one begins to live anew. This is the life of the Blind Beggar. This is the essential eternal life of the World to Come — for constant, unchanging pleasure is not pleasure and not truly called life. Only when one merits to live chiyus chadash each moment — this is the essential long, eternal life the Tzaddikim will merit after the resurrection. This is the aspect of Tefillin.

Even now in this world, the Tzaddikim who truly serve Hashem draw upon themselves eternal life through Torah, tefillah, and ma'asim tovim. Though their entire aspiration is to live always the long life described above — renewing their chiyus with added holiness, new Mochin and new chiyus each moment — nevertheless, it is impossible in this world to live this long life without interruption. The brain must become weary. Therefore one must sleep, and sleep is a great good: by completely withdrawing the Mochin when necessary and sleeping a little, one gives rest to the brain. Through this, one is renewed in the morning and merits to receive new Mochin — to begin living anew.

This is the aspect of Tefillin that one merits in the morning specifically after sleep, as brought in the Kavanos: through the sleep of the night and through awakening at chatzos [midnight] to engage in Torah, the lights of Tefillin emerge in the morning. These are the reshimu [imprint] of yesterday's Mochin that were renewed during the night's sleep. Through this, one afterward receives during tefillah complete, entirely new Mochin — the essential life, the aspect of long life.

Examine the Kavanos and understand well — for all the kavanos of Tefillin are included in our words in a wondrous way, such that each person can receive from them new awakening and wondrous yearning and great, true, and proper counsel at all times for serving the Creator — each person according to his level, his place, and his moment. Even the lowest of the low can remind himself of Hashem at all times, in any place, however he may be.

For now, it is impossible to merit the long life of renewing one's brain and chiyus each moment except through sleep. But the Tzaddikim minimize sleep exceedingly — each one only as much as is necessary for the renewal of the Mochin. Therefore Dovid never slept more than sixty breaths — for he lived the long life described above: new life each moment. He could not sleep more than the barest minimum required for long life.

Therefore the kingship of Dovid is compared to the moon, which renews itself each time — hinting at Kneses Yisrael, the aspect of Malchus Dovid, which is comprised of all Yisrael who must renew their avodah each time, so that they will merit to be renewed in the future and live the long life described above. As we say in Kiddush Levanah: "V'laLevanah amar shetischadesh ateres tiferes la'amusei vaten" — "And to the moon He said that it should renew itself, a crown of glory for those borne from the womb" — who are destined to renew themselves like it, to glorify their Creator on account of the honor of His kingship. Then we say: "Dovid Melech Yisrael chai v'kayam" — for this is the essential chiyus: renewal each time.

Therefore Yisrael counts by the moon, from which the months derive (Chullin 60b) — a hint that we must renew ourselves each time, living new chiyus each day and each moment in serving the Creator. For we never grow old — even if we live a thousand years: "Ki elef shanim b'einecha k'yom esmol" (Tehillim 90:4). All our days are counted by months. Every day of the month is counted toward the month — the 2nd of the month, the 3rd, and so on — and then a new month begins. All our days are counted by "chodesh" [month] — the very word for "new." "Mechadesh chodashim" — "He who renews the months" — "mechadesh" precisely. All the days of Yisrael — the holy nation who received the Torah, which is eternal life ("Ki hu chayecha") — all their days are in the aspect of "chodesh": new chiyus each moment. This is the essential long, eternal life.

All this is merited through Tefillin. Therefore the kingship of Dovid is bound there — in the kesher shel Tefillin. From there descends a holy retzuah to the navel — the beginning of man's chiyus and birth when he enters the air of the world. The beginning of his separation from his mother's womb to begin living on his own is at the cutting of the umbilical cord — then he is separated and begins new life, receiving chiyus independently for the first time.

The essential illumination of Tefillin drawn upon us through the retzuos comes through the brain of the elder who remembers all this — from whom we receive the power to renew our chiyus each time as if born today and having our umbilical cord just cut. From there is drawn the chiyus of man, comprised of seventy years — the days of man's life: "Yemai sh'nosseinu bahem shiv'im shanah" (Tehillim 90:10) — the years of Dovid HaMelech who lived seventy years, corresponding to the seventy faces of Torah, as explained in "Pasach Rabbi Shimon" (LM I:60). All the seventy faces — the chiyus of the seventy years — are drawn from the elders (stories of primordial years), whose illumination reaches us through the youngest elder who draws the renewal of chiyus by virtue of his extraordinarily great brain that remembers even the cutting of the umbilical cord. The Mochin of the deeper elders cannot be revealed outwardly.

This is "Shor'rareich agan hasahar" — the moon that renews itself each time, which is itself the seventy Sanhedrin. They are the seventy faces, the seventy years, received through Tefillin, through the elders, through the retzuah descending to the navel — through which one merits to renew his chiyus each time. This is the essential chiyus of the entire seventy years. For if one does not renew his chiyus each time, he has not truly lived seventy years. The essential chiyus is Avodas Hashem — "Ki hu chayecha." When one does not add holiness and da'as each day, his days are short — who knows if all his seventy years will amount to even a single day? Therefore the complete reshaim who do not keep the Torah at all are called "dead in their lifetime" — for they are truly dead, since they do not keep the Torah which is the essential life. Even one who serves Hashem a little — only the days of his service and good deeds are counted among his days of life. All his chiyus may not amount to more than one day.

But the essential life is the life of Dovid HaMelech, who merited to live seventy complete years in truth — new life each moment. This is why in Kiddush Levanah, regarding the renewal of chiyus (the essence of the moon's renewal = Kneses Yisrael = Malchus Dovid), we say: "...shetischadesh ateres tiferes" — "Ateres Tiferes" precisely = Tefillin, which are called Ateres Tiferes [Crown of Glory], as brought regarding the blessing "Oteir Yisrael b'Sifarah" — "Who crowns Yisrael with glory" — which hints at Tefillin. Through Tefillin is the essential renewal of chiyus = the renewal of the moon.

This is the aspect of the holiness of the bechor — the opening of the first parshah of Tefillin: "Kadeish li chol bechor." One must redeem the bechor from the Kohen to draw the renewal of chiyus and Mochin. The essential Pidyon HaBen [Redemption of the Firstborn] is from ben chodesh [one month old]: "Ufeduyav miben chodesh tifdeh" (Bamidbar 18:16) — "miben chodesh" precisely — for the essential redemption is for the sake of renewal of chiyus, which is the aspect of "chodesh" — "mechadesh chodashim."

For Dovid had no chiyus of his own at all. He was destined to be a nefel [stillbirth]. Only Adam HaRishon gave him seventy years from his own lifespan, as our Sages said. The chiyus of Adam HaRishon was drawn from Arich Anpin — the aspect of Arichas Apayim, the stories of primordial years. As brought in the Writings, the chiyus of the early generations came from Arich Anpin — therefore they lived very long. All the stories the Torah tells about the early generations are aspects of the stories of primordial years — the splendor of the countenance — from which all seventy faces of Torah receive. Therefore the Torah begins with these holy stories before explicating the mitzvos — for all the mitzvos of Torah, comprised in the seventy faces, need to receive from the splendor of the countenance — the beauty of Adam — the stories of primordial years.

The essential chiyus d'Kedushah drawn from there is to renew one's chiyus each moment, to begin living anew. This is "Ani hayom yelidticha" — said about Dovid Mashiach: Dovid merited that the matter was reversed from one extreme to the other. Initially he had no chiyus at all and was destined to be an actual nefel. The matter was reversed and he merited to live seventy years from Adam HaRishon's years — and he lived all seventy years in the aspect of new chiyus each moment, as if he had never yet lived at all. He was at all times like a nefel just now born, having no chiyus of his own, needing to receive new chiyus through Hashem's kindness. And so every moment and instant — and so he lived all seventy years. This is the essential life.

Until through his avodah and toil in this aspect — striving all his days not to sleep away his days but to add holiness and da'as each moment, renewing his chiyus each hour — he merited long and eternal life forever: Dovid Melech Yisrael chai v'kayam. This is the aspect of Tefillin. For Tefillin is from the word "v'niflinu" — "V'niflinu ani v'amecha" — "I and Your people shall be distinguished" (Shemos 33:16) — said when Hashem revealed the Thirteen Attributes = the light of Tefillin = "V'raisa es achorai" = the knot of Tefillin. There is the root of Dovid Mashiach's neshamah — who was destined to be a nefel but now merited to live new life each moment as if born today. This is Tefillin = v'niflinu: the matter was reversed — from nefel to v'niflinu = Tefillin = long life.

Therefore Mashiach is called Bar Nafli [son of the fallen] — for Mashiach will merit the life described above: "Ani hayom yelidticha."

This is: "Someich Hashem l'chol hanoflim" — "Hashem supports all who fall" (Tehillim 145:14). These are those who fall from Avodas Hashem. Hashem supports and awakens them from their sleep through the Tzaddikei HaDor, who are the aspect of Dovid Mashiach — who merited to transform from nefel to long life, beginning to live anew each time. This is Tefillin = v'niflinu. Through this they enliven and sustain all who have fallen, that they should not fall in their minds and not despair of their souls' redemption — until they merit to return to Hashem. Then the fall and descent is itself the ultimate ascent. The essential fall is precisely for the sake of beginning to live anew, as explained elsewhere.

As our Rebbe said (LM I:261): that a person falls from his avodah is from Heaven — for the distancing is the beginning of the drawing close. Therefore he fell so that he would awaken more to draw close to Hashem. His counsel: begin anew to enter Avodas Hashem as if he had never begun at all. This is a great principle in Avodas Hashem — that one must literally begin anew each day. [End of quote.]

Thus precisely through the fall one begins to live anew = Tefillin = the long life of Dovid who was transformed from nefel to long life. This is the aspect of the Geulah that will come through Dovid Mashiach speedily in our days — when Kneses Yisrael will rise from her fall, as our Sages expounded (Berachos 4b) on this verse (for this reason there is no Nun in Ashrei — yet Dovid supported it through Ruach HaKodesh: "Someich Hashem l'chol hanoflim"). In the West they resolve it thus: "She fell and shall not fall again — arise!"

For all the fall of Kneses Yisrael is that Yisrael fall from their avodah — and the Geulah depends on teshuvah (Yoma 86b). The essential support is through Dovid, who lived the long life — through which he enlivens, strengthens, and supports all who fall, so that they don't despair: "Al tismachi oyvasi li, ki nafalti kamti, ki eishev bachoshech Hashem or li" — "Rejoice not over me, my enemy — though I fell, I rose; though I sit in darkness, Hashem is my light" (Michah 7:8).

This is why the Kohen Gadol prayed on Yom HaKippurim in the Beis HaMikdash: "V'lo tapil ishah pri vitnah, v'lo ye'adi avid shultan midveis Yehudah" — "May no woman miscarry, and may the scepter not depart from the house of Yehudah." Both are one: that there should be no actual nefel, nor any fall — and both are merited through the enduring kingship of Dovid, who was transformed from nefel to long life. Yom HaKippurim is the essential teshuvah — rising from the fall (nefel) to renew one's days: "Hashiveinu... chadeish yameinu." After Yom Kippur comes Sukkos = "Akim es Sukkas Dovid hanofales" — "I will raise the fallen booth of Dovid" — nullifying the aspect of nefilah, raising and enlivening through "Someich Hashem l'chol hanoflim." After Sukkos comes Shemini Atzeres = Malchus Dovid: "Zeh ya'atzor b'ami" — "He will restrain My people" (Shmuel I 9:17). As our Rebbe said (LM I:48): then the Nukva restrains the drop so that it should not miscarry — as written in the Kavanos.

This is the aspect of Rosh HaShanah. Rosh HaShanah is the aspect of Tefillin — the renewal one merits each day through sleep, when the Mochin are renewed within emunah — this is Rosh HaShanah, as brought in the Torah "Ashrei ha'am" (LM I:35). Rosh HaShanah is the aspect of the holiness of Eretz Yisrael: "Tamid einei Hashem Elokecha bah, mereishis hashanah v'ad acharis shanah" (Devarim 11:12). This is Tefillin = holiness of Eretz Yisrael = "V'hayah ki yevi'acha" in the parshiyos of Tefillin.

The essential holiness of Rosh HaShanah is that we merit complete teshuvah — it is the first of the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah: to renew the days that passed in darkness and to add holiness and avodah anew. This is: "Chadeish aleinu shanah tovah" — "Chadeish" precisely — that we merit a genuinely new year. Each year is a unique face among the seventy faces of Torah. Therefore each year one must merit entirely new faces — to live new life from now on = long life.

This is why we multiply our prayers on Rosh HaShanah for life — many, many times in each tefillah: "Zachreinu l'chayim... ukesov l'chayim... zocheir yetzurav l'chayim b'rachamim..." For the essential "chayim" is the long life of the Blind Beggar who merited the ultimate memory in perfection — from whom the holiness of Rosh HaShanah is drawn = the holiness of Tefillin = "Ul'zikaron bein einecha." Therefore Rosh HaShanah is called Yom HaZikaron [Day of Remembrance] — for its essential holiness is from the zikaron of the elder. All our requests for life on Rosh HaShanah — our intention is true, eternal life: renewing chiyus each moment. "Chadeish" precisely.

This is the great Chesed Hashem did for us — that He established Rosh HaShanah on Rosh Chodesh. This is a great Chesed, as explained in the Torah "Tik'u I" (LM II). (We also heard more about this from the awesome ma'aseh related to this regarding the kisei [throne], which has not yet been published.) For we need Hashem to renew the year upon us in the aspect of Rosh Chodesh — the renewal of chiyus each time = Malchus Dovid Mashiach.

We greatly request on Rosh HaShanah that His kingship — holy kingship — be revealed. As we say many times: "V'simloch... umoloch..." and "Va'arichas ner l'ven Yishai meshichecha u'tzmichas keren l'Dovid avdecha bimheirah v'yameinu." The kingship of Mashiach is the long life we request on Rosh HaShanah = Kiddush HaChodesh. Therefore He established Rosh HaShanah on Rosh Chodesh.

This is what our Sages said regarding Rosh HaShanah being on Rosh Chodesh: "One zikaron rises for both" — "zikaron" precisely. The holiness of Rosh HaShanah (= Rosh Chodesh) — to renew the year with new chiyus = long life — all this is the aspect of zikaron.

This is also explained in the words of our Rebbe (LM II:40), beginning "Mi she'yode'a mei'Eretz Yisrael" — where it is explained that Tefillin, Eretz Yisrael, and Rosh HaShanah are one aspect.

Behold, the sum total of Tefillin is the aspect of Mochin Chayim [living brains]: to begin living anew each time — whether Tzaddik, beinoni, or rasha. As long as the name Yisrael is called upon him, he must begin anew each day. This is: "V'atem had'veikim BaHashem Elokeichem — chayim kulchem hayom" — "You who cling to Hashem your G-d — you are all alive today" (Devarim 4:4) — said regarding the holy Tefillin. "Chayim kulchem hayom" — "hayom" precisely — one must renew chiyus each and every day as if beginning to live today.

This is the aspect of Tefillin shel Yad and Tefillin shel Rosh. It is brought in the Kavanos that Tefillin shel Rosh are the aspect of three Names: Ehyeh Havayah Ehyeh, which have the numerical value of Chayim [= 68] — the aspect of Mochin. And Tefillin shel Yad are the Mochin of Malchus — therefore they are three Names: Ehyeh Havayah Adnus, which equal Yabok [= 112].

It is explained there that the light of Tefillin emerges through the sleep of the night, when the Mochin are renewed within emunah (= Malchus). By arising at chatzos and mourning the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash and engaging in Torah — through this, the point of Malchus-emunah, which descended during the night to all the lower worlds to extract holy sparks (the neshamos who fell through their sins, to instill in them hirhurei teshuvah and raise them and return them to Hashem) — is raised up. The Tzaddikim and G-d-fearing, through Tikun Chatzos and Torah study at night, raise the point of Malchus until it ascends at dawn and sits on the left arm — its place. Then Z'eir Anpin shines into it the reshimu of its Mochin that remained in his heart — for the essential Mochin d'Gadlus exist only during tefillah; afterward they depart, leaving only the reshimu. This is the light of Tefillin — the reshimu of the Mochin remaining all day. At night, even the reshimu departs — therefore there are no Tefillin at night. The reshimu of Malchus's Mochin also departs at night, except that this reshimu does not depart completely — it remains in the heart: "Simeini k'chosam al libecha, k'chosam al zero'echa" — "Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm" (Shir HaShirim 8:6).

Then in the morning, he shines the reshimu into her on the left arm — this is Tefillin shel Yad. When Z'eir Anpin sees that she already has her Tefillin — the reshimu of the Mochin — he is aroused with kinah [jealousy]: "Kashah kaSh'ol kinah" — "Jealousy is fierce as the grave." Then he takes back his own Mochin — the reshimu renewed during the night — and this is Tefillin shel Rosh.

Thus: Tefillin shel Rosh = the shining of the Mochin of Da'as (Z'eir Anpin). Tefillin shel Yad = the shining of the Mochin of Malchus (emunah). The essential Tefillin, Mochin, and chiyus are drawn through the true Tzaddikei HaDor — the Mochin and chiyus of the entire world. Each Tzaddik HaDor is the aspect of Moshe-Mashiach. Moshe is the Da'as — the Tefillin-Mochin. As our Rebbe said (LM I:38): the true Tzaddik is the aspect of the river that goes out from Eden to water the Garden — "Umisham yipared v'hayah l'arba'ah rashim" — "And from there it divides into four heads" = the four parshiyos of Tefillin. The Mochin of Tefillin are drawn through the river from Eden = the true Tzaddik.

Tefillin shel Rosh = the Tzaddik himself, the aspect of Z'eir Anpin. Tefillin shel Yad = Kneses Yisrael, Malchus. That is: the Tzaddik's own Mochin = shel Rosh. The Mochin of Klal Yisrael, whom the Tzaddik illuminates and draws close to Hashem = shel Yad — whose essence is emunah, the foundation upon which everything depends: "Ba Chavakuk v'he'emidan al achas — v'Tzaddik be'emunaso yichyeh!" — "Chavakuk came and established them on one — and the righteous shall live by his faith!" (Makkos 24a).

The Tzaddik must withdraw his Mochin — even the reshimu departs during sleep — and nothing remains but the reshimu of the Mochin of emunah remaining in his heart ("k'chosam al libecha"). Then during sleep, emunah contracts to a point and descends to all the lower worlds to extract sparks — the neshamos who fell through their sins. For them, the Tzaddik must lower himself and withdraw his Da'as in order to instill in them complete emunah and bring them close to the holy emunah and return them to Hashem. All this is the Tzaddik's "sleep" — as understood from our Rebbe's words: that when the Tzaddik engages in mundane conversation and stories, this is the aspect of sleep for him. It is all for the sake of raising and lifting the world to draw them close to Hashem. Since they cannot receive from the Tzaddik's Moach directly, he must withdraw his Da'as, contract himself to a point, and extract and raise them through the point of emunah alone.

Afterward, when he awakens from sleep with all the sparks and neshamos he has raised and awakened to Hashem — they must engage in Torah, tefillah, and Avodas Hashem until they merit to ascend to their place, in the aspect of Tefillin shel Yad — Kneses Yisrael sitting on the left arm. Then all the reshimu of all the Mochin of Klal Yisrael, which had departed but remained in the Tzaddik's heart ("k'chosam al libecha") — he shines everything into the point of emunah that ascended with all the extractions (the neshamos of the ba'alei teshuvah whom he raised and returned to Hashem). He shines Da'as and seichel into them to strengthen them in complete emunah, so that they strengthen their avodah and do not look at the hindrances of the Baal Davar and other obstacles, but pass over everything through the strength of their emunah that was greatly strengthened through the Da'as he shone into them — the aspect of Tefillin shel Yad. Through this, yad keihah — all the hindrances drawn from Gevuros and dinim — is sweetened. Through the strength of emunah, they pass over everything — nothing can make them fall. He shines into them the Da'as of holy emunah: knowing that Hashem is in every place and there is no obstacle in the world that cannot be broken and there is no despair in the world at all.

When the Tzaddik sees that the point of emunah has succeeded and borne fruit — that it has already received Mochin and Da'as (= Tefillin shel Yad), i.e. his efforts have succeeded, having illuminated Da'as in the souls he raised and drew close to Hashem until they are strong in their emunah to stand their ground and pass over all obstacles — then the Tzaddik himself is aroused with kinah for his students. Seeing that they have received true Mochin and Da'as from him, he is aroused with jealousy — in the aspect of "Umitalmidai yoser mikulam" — "From my students more than from all." Through the students in whom he shone the Moach and Da'as of holy emunah (Kneses Yisrael = Tefillin shel Yad), he is aroused with jealousy and remembers: "Where are my own Mochin?" Then he takes back the reshimu of his Mochin that had departed during sleep — and receives this reshimu renewed with wondrous novelty. This is Tefillin shel Rosh.

As explained in our Rebbe's words elsewhere: first the Tzaddik lowers himself to draw close souls, and afterward he returns to his level with added illumination. From these two aspects — the Tzaddik's own Mochin and the Mochin of emunah that he instills in Kneses Yisrael — are drawn Tefillin shel Rosh and Tefillin shel Yad for each and every individual, for every aspect includes all aspects.

This is: "Lam'natze'ach l'Dovid l'hazkir" (Tehillim 70:1) — "l'hazkir" — to remind himself, as Rashi explains there: a parable of a king who was angry at his flock... afterward he returned the flock... That is: first the Tzaddik reminds Yisrael to return to Hashem; then, when he sees that his prayer and toil have succeeded and he has returned Yisrael to Hashem — then he reminds himself. This is Tefillin shel Rosh — the aspect of zikaron.

Therefore the Mochin of Tefillin shel Rosh are the aspect of Ehyeh Havayah Ehyeh, which have the numerical value of Chayim. For Ehyeh is the aspect of ibur [gestation], as explained in the Kavanos. As explained in the words of our Rebbe in the Torah "Kera es Yehoshua" (LM I:6): Ehyeh is the aspect of teshuvah — "Ana zamin l'meihevei" — "I am preparing to become." Before teshuvah, one has no havayah [existence/being] at all. Only when one begins to do teshuvah is he in the aspect of Ehyeh — "Ana zamin l'meihevei" — he begins to prepare himself to have being in the world.

One must do teshuvah upon teshuvah. Even a Tzaddik who has already done complete teshuvah must do teshuvah each time regarding his previous hasagah [perception] — for each time he comes to a new hasagah. Then he does teshuvah — the aspect of Ehyeh — upon yesterday's hasagah, for he had materialized the loftiness of Hashem's G-dliness. This is the aspect of Shabbos — the World to Come, which is entirely Shabbos, entirely teshuvah.

Thus the true Tzaddik is always in the aspect of Ehyeh — for each time he comes to new Mochin, beginning to perceive Hashem with new perception, which is the long life of living anew each time. Each day he is in the aspect of Ehyeh — "Ana zamin l'meihevei" — as if he has not yet begun to live at all and has had no havayah in the world. Only now does he begin to live and prepare himself to have being. This is Ehyeh.

Therefore Tefillin — long life where the Tzaddik begins anew each time — are in the aspect of Ehyeh Havayah Ehyeh = Chayim. Each day: Ehyeh (= ibur, "ana zamin l'meihevei," beginning to live as if he had no havayah or chiyus at all) → then new complete Mochin are drawn = Havayah (= the Mochin) → immediately upon receiving these Mochin (= life), he withdraws them; only the reshimu remains; then he yearns again to receive even greater new Mochin = second Ehyeh ("ana zamin l'meihevei"). And so forever. These three Names = Chayim = the essential long life.

But the Mochin of Kneses Yisrael — Tefillin shel Yad — are the aspect of Ehyeh Havayah Adnus. They too must begin anew each day (= Ehyeh), then receive their Mochin (= Havayah). But when their Mochin depart, they remain in the aspect of Adnus — Malchus, emunah — believing that Hashem is Adon Kol [Master of all]. This point of Adnus/emunah never departs — the reshimu of the Mochin of emunah must always remain. For the common people, the essential renewal of Mochin is so that they remain in strong emunah — which is their essential chiyus, the foundation of everything.

But the Mochin of Tefillin shel Rosh — the Tzaddik's own Mochin — remain in the aspect of Ehyeh: he merits the true long life of beginning anew each time. This is Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh — teshuvah upon teshuvah. Each time he begins to live anew in the aspect of Ehyeh. "Ehyeh" = "Ana zamin l'meihevei" — beginning to live and receive new Mochin = Tefillin. "Asher" = letters of "Rosh" = the Mochin = Havayah. Then he returns to Ehyeh — yearning to receive even greater new chiyus and Mochin. Thus Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh = Ehyeh Havayah Ehyeh = Tefillin. This Name was revealed to Moshe at the time of Yetzias Mitzrayim — the aspect of Tefillin.

Likewise, each individual must draw upon himself these two aspects of Mochin: shel Yad and shel Rosh. When the Mochin depart, through the reshimu of emunah remaining in the heart, one draws Da'as and Mochin to strengthen himself in emunah = Tefillin shel Yad (whose Names = Yabok = baki = passing over all obstacles). Then one is aroused with kinah for himself and draws great Mochin to rise from level to level, living new chiyus each time = Tefillin shel Rosh (whose Names = Ehyeh Havayah Ehyeh = Chayim). Understand well.

This is the aspect of Tefillin of Rashi and Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam. It is explained in the Kavanos that Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam are far loftier Mochin, where the Gevuros [judgments] emerge before the Chassadim [kindnesses] — the order of Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam: Yud-Kei-Kuf-Vav (= Kadeish, V'hayah ki yevi'acha, V'hayah im shamoa, Shema). Tefillin of Rashi are Havayah in proper order — Chassadim before Gevuros.

For at first it arose in Hashem's thought to create the world with Middas HaDin [the Attribute of Justice] alone. He saw the world could not endure and He placed Middas HaRachamim [Mercy] first, combining it with Din: "Eileh toldos hashamayim v'ha'aretz b'hibar'am b'yom asos Hashem Elokim eretz v'shamayim" (Bereishis 2:4).

The Yetzer HaRa and the Sitra Achra are drawn from the Gevuros and Dinim originating in the initial Tzimtzum of the Chalal HaPanui [Empty Space]. Breaking the Yetzer HaRa comes from Middas HaRachamim that was combined with Din — giving power to break the Yetzer HaRa and transform it to holiness. This is what the Tzaddikim do: transform Din to Rachamim.

At first, Hashem wanted man to overcome the Yetzer HaRa by his own power, without heavenly assistance — Din alone. But He saw this was impossible, so He placed Rachamim before Din. From this comes Hashem's constant mercy — sending hirhurei teshuvah and assisting man to break the Yetzer HaRa. As our Sages said (Kiddushin 30b): "Each day a man's Yetzer overpowers him — were it not that Hashem helps him, he would fall into its hands." The Yetzer overpowering each day = the Din of the initial thought being aroused each day. But Hashem immediately has mercy and places Rachamim before Din = the help and assistance.

However, there are great Tzaddikim who do not need heavenly assistance. Hashem conducts Himself with them initially with Middas HaDin, and they withstand all trials, enduring all manner of suffering and troubles drawn from Din, and remain steadfast. As it says about Avraham and the Avos: "HaElokim asher hishalchu avosai lefanav" (Bereishis 48:15) — "HaElokim" precisely = Middas HaDin, walking on his own without heavenly assistance, as Rashi explains in Parshas Noach.

This is the suffering of the Tzaddikim: "Hashem Tzaddik yivchan" — "Hashem tests the righteous" (Tehillim 11:5) — like a flax worker: the better his flax, the harder he strikes it (Bereishis Rabbah 32). "Ki es asher ye'ehav Hashem yochiach" — "Whom Hashem loves, He rebukes" (Mishlei 3:12). They sweeten the Din at its root in the initial thought. They believe and know that the suffering and Dinim themselves are great goods. Through this they merit to ascend and be included in the initial thought.

This is the aspect of Rabbi Akiva, whose flesh was combed with iron combs. Moshe Rabbeinu asked: "This is Torah and this is its reward?!" Hashem answered: "Silence! Thus it arose in the thought." The suffering of such Tzaddikim is drawn from the initial thought — creating through Din alone — so they would merit to stand the trial without heavenly assistance and thereby be included in the initial thought.

For the essential Din is drawn from the initial Tzimtzum of the Chalal HaPanui. As explained in the Torah "Bo el Paroh" (LM I:64): the Chalal HaPanui is the aspect of the questions that cannot be answered. But the great Tzaddik — the aspect of Moshe — can enter even these questions, the Chalal HaPanui. This is the Tzaddik ascending to the initial thought — the beginning of the Tzimtzum, the root of Din — and withstanding the trial there, enduring all suffering and Dinim. Through this he merits to perceive the secret of the Chalal HaPanui: that even there, Hashem is concealed and hidden in a wondrous and awesome manner that cannot be grasped, as written there.

This is the aspect of Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — loftier Mochin where Gevuros precede Chassadim — drawn from these higher Tzaddikim. Hashem conducts Himself with them through the initial thought. They merit to be included in the initial thought and sweeten everything at its root. This is "Gevuros before Chassadim": they can receive the Gevuros themselves before Chassadim — the conduct of the initial thought — for they merit even through Middas HaDin itself, having endured great suffering and been tested.

But Tefillin of Rashi — Chassadim before Gevuros — is the aspect of placing Rachamim before Din, which is the essential conduct of the entire world. Therefore the main Tefillin are those of Rashi, which most of the world wears — for the world's essential conduct and endurance is only through this. But one who wishes to sanctify himself with additional holiness should also wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — to receive illumination from those higher Tzaddikim who merited to ascend to the initial thought and sweeten all Dinim at their very root.

Therefore our Rebbe instructed his followers to wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam. For all distancing from Hashem comes from the Yetzer HaRa whose root is in Middas HaDin drawn from the Chalal HaPanui. The essential additional holiness is drawn through Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — from the Tzaddikim who ascend to the root of Din in the Chalal HaPanui and sweeten everything at its root. Through this, power is drawn for all who are far away to break and nullify the Yetzer HaRa drawn from there.

Therefore now, in the Ikvesa d'Meshicha [the heels of Mashiach's footsteps], at the end of the galus, one must be very careful to wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam, as all the true Tzaddikim of our days urged. For now the Baal Davar has strengthened exceedingly — seeing that his end is near, he exerts all his power, like two men wrestling: when one sees he is about to fall, he rallies with all his strength to topple the other. As the wise man said: "There is no warrior like the desperate one."

The galus is the aspect of ibur [gestation]; leaving the galus = leidah [birth]. As with Geulas Mitzrayim, which is called birth: "Umolodosayich b'yom huleches osach" (Yechezkel 16:4). And regarding the final Geulah: "Ki chalah gam yaldah Tziyon es baneha" — "For Tziyon has travailed and also given birth to her children" (Yeshayah 66:8). Therefore at the end of the galus, the galus intensifies — as in Mitzrayim: "Umei'az basi el Paroh l'daber bismecha heira la'am hazeh" — "Tichbad ha'avodah" (Shemos 5:22-23). This is kishui holadah [difficult labor] — "Vayhi ki hikshah Paroh l'shalcheinu" (Shemos 13:15).

All the suffering endured now at the end of this final galus are the aspect of chevlei leidah [birth pangs]: "K'mo harah sakriv laledes tachil tiz'ak bachavaleha." The essential intensification of the galus is that the Baal Davar strengthens mightily over the souls of Yisrael to distance them from Hashem. This is the essential galus — the suffering of the nefesh. Beyond this, everything is hevel. The essential trouble is that he introduces kefiros and apikorsus into the world. As our Rebbe said: "A great apikorsus is going through the world." As we see with our own eyes — never was there such apikorsus in Yisrael as now, when the brazen ones among the nation teach the youth their wisdoms and their languages.

All this intensification of the Baal Davar is the aspect of Chevlei Mashiach = chevlei leidah. All his power derives from the root of Din in the Chalal HaPanui. Therefore now the only power to stand against him is through the great true Tzaddikim who can enter the Chalal HaPanui and sweeten the Din at its root — nullifying all the power of the Yetzer HaRa of all the world's inhabitants drawn from there. Therefore each person must be careful to wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — drawn from the Mochin of these great Tzaddikim — to receive power from them to break the Yetzer HaRa that is strengthening so greatly now.

For the essential kishui holadah derives from Amalek, as understood from our Rebbe's words (LM I:135) on the verse "Vay'shasef Shmuel es Agag" — how Shmuel cut Agag into four, through which the womb of the woman with kishui holadah was opened. Amalek = the kefiros and apikorsus drawn from the Chalal HaPanui. Therefore he is called "Reishis" — "Reishis goyim Amalek" (Bamidbar 24:20) — for the Chalal HaPanui preceded the world (without it there would be no place for creation). From there comes the kelipah that precedes the fruit. Therefore Amalek is called Reishis — his power from the Chalal HaPanui that preceded the world.

This is the firstborn right of Eisav, who is Amalek — from the kelipos drawn from the Chalal HaPanui that preceded the world. Therefore Yaakov strove to take the bechorah from Eisav — for in truth Hashem preceded everything: He fills all worlds and surrounds all worlds, and He Himself created the Chalal HaPanui for the sake of creation. Through their emunah in Hashem who preceded everything, Yisrael pass over all the wisdoms and kefiros and apikorsus that come from the Chalal HaPanui — believing that even within the Chalal HaPanui itself, Hashem is concealed. He preceded everything. Therefore Yisrael are called Ivri'im — through their faith in the G-d of the Ivri'im, they pass over all the wisdoms that come from the Chalal HaPanui. Therefore Yisrael are truly the firstborn: "B'ni bechori Yisrael" (Shemos 4:22).

Yaakov took the bechorah from Eisav. Initially the bechorah had to be with Eisav — for the kelipah precedes the fruit, and his firstborn right derived from the Chalal HaPanui that preceded the world. But Yaakov, through his emunah, merited to pass over the Chalal HaPanui and believe and be included in Hashem who preceded everything. Afterward he nullified Eisav's bechorah (= Reishis goyim Amalek) and took it for himself, until his offspring were all called bechorim: "B'ni bechori Yisrael."

This is the Makkas Bechoros at the time of Yetzias Mitzrayim, when the firstborn of Yisrael were sanctified. For all the exiles — included in Galus Mitzrayim — derive from the contamination of Amalek (= the essential contamination of the serpent = Reishis goyim), from whom all four kingdoms receive, as our Rebbe said in the Torah "Mishra d'Sakina" (LM I:30). The prince of Mitzrayim is Edom = Eisav. Paroh's hardness and heaviness of heart — refusing to let Yisrael leave — came from the apikorsus and kefiros drawn from the Chalal HaPanui = Amalek. Therefore Hashem killed all the firstborn of Mitzrayim — to subdue the bechor of the Sitra Achra drawn from Eisav's firstborn right (= the kefiros from the Chalal HaPanui that preceded the world) — and to elevate the firstborn of Yisrael, who receive from Yaakov's bechorah based on emunah that passes over the Chalal HaPanui.

Through this, Yisrael left Mitzrayim (= birth). Then the firstborn were sanctified to be given to the Kohen — who receives his holiness from the holy elder, the aspect of z'kan Aharon — Tikkunei D'ikna drawn through the Blind Beggar who was included in the Ein Sof that preceded everything (where the whole world does not amount to the blink of an eye). This sanctifies the firstborn — first birth — drawing the holiness of bechorah of Yisrael, which is emunah. "V'ha'avarta kol peter rechem LaHashem" — "V'ha'avarta" precisely — through the holiness of the firstborn, one passes over the Chalal HaPanui via emunah.

Therefore the parshiyos of Tefillin speak of Yetzias Mitzrayim, the holiness of the firstborn, and emunah — for they are all one. Through emunah one passes over all the wisdoms from the Chalal HaPanui. This = Yetzias Mitzrayim = holiness of the firstborn. From there come the essential Tefillin — the renewal of Mochin and chiyus. The essential renewal of Mochin and chiyus is received through emunah — the essential life: "B'or pnei melech chayim" (Mishlei 16:15). Through emunah in Chidush HaOlam [the Creation of the world] — that Hashem created everything as He willed, yesh mei'ayin hamuchlat [something from absolute nothing] — just as He renewed the world from absolute nothingness, so too He renews now in His goodness each day, constantly, Ma'aseh Bereishis. The essential daily renewal of Ma'aseh Bereishis is through Chochmah: "Kulam b'Chochmah asisa" (Tehillim 104:24) — the new Mochin drawn each day to recognize His light anew. "Uvtuvo mechadesh b'chol yom tamid ma'aseh Bereishis" — "Ain tov ela Torah, ain tov ela Tzaddik" — the true Tzaddik merits new Torah perception and Da'as each day, through which Ma'aseh Bereishis is renewed. From there: the essential Tefillin.

For truly it is all one: the birth of a Jewish nefesh and the nullification of kishui holadah in the physical sense is literally the aspect of Yetzias Mitzrayim (= birth), after Hashem nullified kishui holadah through Makkas Bechoros. For at Yetzias Mitzrayim (= birth), the holy emunah was revealed — emunas Chidush HaOlam — through the awesome signs and wonders Hashem performed.

Each new Jewish nefesh that is born is a new revelation and new Da'as to recognize the One who spoke and the world came into being. For Hashem never does the same thing twice — as our Rebbe said: even reincarnated neshamos do not return identically, for Hashem never repeats. Each birth = a new seichel to know Hashem with new knowledge. In each generation His G-dliness is revealed with new recognition. For this Hashem "troubles Himself" from generation to generation — to purify the neshamos more and more from the serpent's contamination. "Zeh Shmi l'olam v'zeh zichri l'dor dor" — "L'dor vador yeshabach ma'asecha."

Therefore each time a new nefesh comes — new seichel and new knowledge to recognize Him, to reveal His emunah further — the contamination of Amalek (the serpent's contamination) is aroused and seeks to obstruct the birth. This is kishui holadah — through the serpent's contamination (Adam's sin: "B'etzev teildi vanim"). Our Rebbe said that Mizmor l'Sodah is an effective remedy for a woman in difficult labor — because it speaks of emunah: "De'u ki Hashem Hu Elokim," ending: "V'ad dor vador emunaso." The essential emunah is renewed and strengthened from generation to generation through the renewal of neshamos (= new intelligences recognizing Hashem). Therefore through emunah, kishui holadah is nullified. The main remedy is tefillah = emunah.

"Milchamah LaHashem ba'Amalek midor dor" — "midor dor" precisely — he intensifies in each generation. He is an old and foolish king, not wanting the renewal of Mochin and chiyus that comes through the renewal of neshamos each generation. He denies Chidush HaOlam. Therefore the parshiyos of Tefillin begin with birth — "Kadeish li chol bechor" — for birth = the renewal of Mochin and chiyus = Tefillin: to renew one's brain and chiyus each day, beginning Avodas Hashem anew each day.

Therefore now, at the end of the galus — when the Baal Davar intensifies exceedingly (= the contamination of the serpent, Haman-Amalek, Chevlei Mashiach = chevlei leidah = kishui holadah) — the birth pangs and difficult labor are now far heavier than at Geulas Mitzrayim, because now the final Geulah will come — a complete Geulah with no galus after it. Then the serpent's contamination will be completely nullified, all Yisrael will return to Hashem in truth forever, until we merit Techiyas HaMeisim, when the world will be renewed: "Bila hamaves lanetzach" — "Death will be swallowed up forever" (Yeshayah 25:8). Then we will live long, eternal life = Tefillin = Eitz HaChayim.

Because the Baal Davar sees his end approaching, he intensifies exceedingly. His essential strategy is to make Yisrael fall into spiritual ziknah [old age / exhaustion]: as if we have already grown old in this long galus of so many hundreds of years, and there is no more hope. He causes each individual to fall into this ziknah: as if one has already aged in his deeds and can no longer return. But the essential Geulah depends on teshuvah, as the Zohar HaKadosh says: "This matter depends on nothing but teshuvah."

We pray: "Al tashlicheinu l'eis ziknah, kichlos kocheinu al ta'azveinu" — "Cast us not away in the time of old age; when our strength fails, forsake us not" (Tehillim 71:9) — that we should not fall into the ziknah of the Sitra Achra. The Baal Davar (Haman-Amalek) is called an old and foolish king — denying Chidush HaOlam. From this denial comes the ziknah of the Sitra Achra — as if the physical world is old and aged from long ago. The serpent said to Chavah: "Min ha'eitz achal uvara es ha'olam" — "From the Tree He ate and created the world" (Rashi, Bereishis 3:5) — denying Chidush HaOlam. Through this, death was decreed — the opposite of long life.

The elders who lack completeness — who do not add holiness and da'as each day — give strength to these kefiros (= the metzach hanachash [forehead of the serpent], as in LM II:4). Since they do not add holiness and give foothold to the ziknah of the Sitra Achra, the kefiros of the serpent's forehead — denying Chidush HaOlam — are strengthened. All these kefiros, from which the essential Yetzer HaRa intensifies now at the end of the galus, derive from the Chalal HaPanui — from which come all the questions of the philosophers that cannot be answered, all the apikorsus and kefiros, and the root of all evil desires. For the root of all evil desire is eil acher — kefiros, as our Rebbe explained.

Therefore one must wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — the Mochin drawn from the Tzaddikim who can enter the initial Tzimtzum of the Chalal HaPanui, sweeten the Din there, and reveal Hashem's G-dliness — informing humanity that even the Chalal HaPanui and all the questions and kefiros themselves derive from Hashem, who sustains everything. It is impossible to know Him except through the absence of knowledge that preceded knowledge — the questions of the Chalal HaPanui, the withdrawal of Da'as (His light that was withdrawn from the Chalal HaPanui) — in order to create a place for the world, so that His G-dliness could be revealed in the world, as fully explained in "Bo el Paroh."

Therefore one must place emunah before the world — this is the essence. Through this, one breaks the kelipah that precedes the fruit (= the Chalal HaPanui that preceded the world). Through emunah, one passes over everything. This is also the ma'abarta of Tefillin — through Tefillin (= renewal of Mochin merited through emunah), one passes over everything. When one is strong in emunah for many years, serving Hashem through emunah alone, one merits afterward to know and perceive Hashem with a wondrous knowledge that comes through emunah — in the aspect of matei v'lo matei [reaching and not reaching]. This is "Lachazos b'no'am Hashem ul'vaker b'Heichalo" — "To gaze at the pleasantness of Hashem and to visit His Sanctuary" (Tehillim 27:4) — which Dovid HaMelech requested all his days.

Therefore our essential hope now — to leave this bitter galus, to nullify the kishui holadah of the Geulah (intensifying now collectively and individually for each person seeking the holy path) — rests on the power of the Tzaddikim, the Mochin of Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam (very great Mochin). Therefore now one must be especially careful to wear Tefillin of Rabbeinu Tam — to hasten the Geulah collectively and individually, speedily in our days. Each person must merit the redemption of his soul from this bitter galus of havlei olam hazeh. One must endure actual chevlei leidah and kishui holadah, especially in the beginning — crying many cries and groans of "Ach!" and "Avoi!" and many turns and twists — before meriting to give birth to the holiness of one's nefesh and redeem it from galus. May it be fulfilled speedily: "Rani akarah lo yaladah" (Yeshayah 54:1); "Ha'ani ashbir v'lo olid... ki chalah gam yaldah Tziyon es baneha" (Yeshayah 66:9) — speedily in our days, Amen.

This is why "Uva l'Tziyon Go'el" is juxtaposed to Mizmor "Ya'ancha". It is explained in the Kavanos that Mizmor Ya'ancha is recited to give birth to the Mochin and shefa and draw them into this world. Therefore there are seventy words in Mizmor Ya'ancha — corresponding to the seventy cries the woman in labor must cry before giving birth.

The Geulah = birth, which comes after chevlei leidah = Chevlei Mashiach. The chevlei leidah are seventy cries — for the essential birth is the birth of the Mochin: to renew one's avodah and awaken from sleep (= ibur). Therefore they are seventy cries — corresponding to the seventy faces of Torah = the totality of Mochin that must be birthed and drawn, to awaken from one's sleep and fall, to regain all the seventy faces one has lost, and to begin living anew. This is the essential Geulah, individually and collectively. "Uva l'Tziyon Go'el ul'shavei fesha b'Yaakov" — "ul'shavei fesha" precisely = the ba'alei teshuvah who renew the days that passed in darkness = renewal of chiyus: "Hashiveinu Hashem eilecha v'nashuvah, chadeish yameinu k'kedem." After Mizmor Ya'ancha (= chevlei leidah), we say "Uva l'Tziyon Go'el" — speedily in our days, Amen.

Therefore Tefillin must be written on the hide of a kosher animal specifically (Shulchan Aruch, Siman 32, Se'if 12). For the hide [or] is the aspect of the medameh [imaginative faculty] — the external garment of the intellect. There are Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah — the three inner lights — the three Mochin. Corresponding to them are three keilim [vessels]: flesh, sinews, and bones. Over them all is the hide that covers — chitzoniyus d'chitzoniyus [the externality of externality], katnus d'katnus [the smallness of smallness].

(As explained at length in Eitz Chayim, Sha'ar HaChashmal, regarding the hide, the Chashmal, and Nogah — the aspect of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil. They are all one category and draw sustenance from each other. There the essential work of birur [refinement] takes place — to purify the hide from the grip of the kelipos. The essential refinement is of Kelipas Nogah = Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil = the hide that garments the entire body. Its purification is through the Chashmal — to transform "kasnos or" [garments of hide, with Ayin] into "kasnos or" [garments of light, with Alef].)

This hide — the external vessel of the body — corresponds to the medameh — the external power of the intellect. The medameh is the animalistic power, the life-force of the animal aspect within man. It is the externality of the intellect. There, in the medameh, is where the essential birur takes place. As the medameh is purified, so one merits emunah — which is the ultimate completeness of the medameh's rectification, as explained in "Tik'u 3" (LM II:8) and above in Hilchos Tzitzis: the essential emunah resides in the medameh.

This is the aspect of Dovid as the fourth leg of the Merkavah — the fourth letter of the Name — the aspect of the Shin of three heads and the Shin of four heads. The first three letters = tlas avahan [three Patriarchs] = the three Mochin = Shin of three heads. Dovid = the final letter of the Name = Malchus/emunah — corresponding to the rectification of the medameh = the Shin of four heads.

The essential confusion of the medameh — which includes all foreign thoughts, evil fantasies, philosophical inquiries, questions, kefiros, apikorsus, and all varieties of thoughts that confuse and distort a person away from Hashem and from true Tzaddikim — all this comes from an unpurified medameh, from the Chalal HaPanui where all the kelipos take hold, and their primary grip is in the medameh (= the Tree of Knowledge).

Therefore Sifrei Torah, Tefillin, and Mezuzos are written on hide specifically — to purify the medameh and merit complete emunah. The essential purification of the medameh is through Ruach Nevuah [the spirit of prophecy] = the totality of Torah, as in "Tik'u." This = the totality of writing STA"M [Sifrei Torah, Tefillin, Mezuzos] = the Torah's parshiyos = Ruach Nevuah. Therefore they must be written on hide.

They must be written on the hide of a kosher animal specifically — for the animal itself is the aspect of the medameh, and the hide of an animal = the ultimate chitzoniyus d'chitzoniyus of the medameh. There the essential birur takes place through writing Tefillin and Sifrei Torah. For Tefillin are such great Mochin that they have the power to purify and rectify the very lowest externality of the medameh. The greater the Tzaddik, the more he can purify the lowest and most external levels. Through this, all worlds are rectified, all sparks and all fallen neshamos are elevated.

This is the aspect of the holy elders of the story: the youngest of them remembered the cutting of his umbilical cord — the beginning of katnus. To remember what happened then = the purification of the hide, which is the connection between mother and child through the navel — only hide. For the chain of all worlds, from world to world, proceeds from the navel downward, as explained in Eitz Chayim (Sha'ar HaNekudim) — each lower world begins at the navel of the upper world (Netzach-Hod-Yesod = the "legs" of the upper world, from which the lower world receives its chiyus). Therefore Hashem created the physical reality that the fetus is connected via the navel to its mother — for the chain from generation to generation begins from the navel downward.

Therefore the essential drawing of Mochin from the holy elders comes through the youngest elder (= the first from below upward) who remembered the cutting of the navel. From there the essential revelation of Mochin and the chain of worlds flows downward — the aspect of the retzuos of Tefillin that extend to the navel.

Yet in truth, although we receive light only from the navel downward (through the youngest elder), all the Mochin and chiyus we receive are drawn only through the power of the highest elder — the Blind Beggar (= the Baby). For it is impossible to fashion keilim to receive the light below without extremely exalted holiness and very lofty light. As our Rebbe said in "Mishra d'Sakina" (LM I:30): perception of G-dliness can only be received through many contractions, from cause to effect, from a higher intellect to a lower intellect. The lower a person's level and the sicker his soul, the greater the Rebbe he needs — a craftsman and healer able to fashion keilim to place within him perceptions of G-dliness.

As explained in Eitz Chayim (Sha'ar HaNekudim): the light of the keilim is drawn specifically from a very high place. The higher the source of the light received by the keilim, the less shevirah [breakage] occurs — for the higher the light, the more it can contract itself and introduce light gradually, in measured doses, in the aspect of matei v'lo matei, ratzo vashov, in a wondrous and awesome manner. This is Olam HaTikun drawn from Atik — the root of all the elders.

Therefore the highest elder was blind — no histakulus [gazing] at this world at all = tikun ha'einayim. From him all elders draw — the eight parshiyos of Tefillin — down to the youngest elder who remembered the navel-cutting, through whom the essential Tefillin light is drawn to us. As in Eitz Chayim (Sha'ar HaNekudim): the light of the eyes is revealed from the navel downward — the Oros HaNekudim descended from the eyes, received lights from the shiboles [channel] of the beard, and were revealed from the navel downward — the beginning of keilim formation. The essential purpose of keilim formation = to fashion vessels and contractions to perceive Hashem.

This elder who sanctified his eyes and sealed them from the sight of this world = the rectification of p'gam ha'einayim [damage to the eyes] = the damage of all sins in the Torah (= Sheviras HaKeilim). For all sins come through p'gam ha'einayim: "V'lo sasuru acharei l'vavchem v'acharei eineichem" (Bamidbar 15:39). As our Sages said (Yerushalmi Berachos 1): "Liba v'eina t'rei sarsurai d'aveirah" — "The heart and the eye are two agents of sin." Therefore this elder who sanctified his eyes = the essential rectification of Sheviras HaKeilim. He is the highest elder = Atik, through whom the essential tikun comes.

Therefore the essential Tefillin are on the hide — chitzoniyus d'chitzoniyus, the ultimate barrier between being and being, between world and world. Through the pores of the hide, light breaks through from world to world. We write the holy parshiyos of Tefillin — the holy and awesome Names, 42 Azkaros — on physical animal hide. We draw light from the most exalted height down to the most physical keilim (= chitzoniyus d'chitzoniyus = the hide). Through this specifically, we can receive the light of perceiving G-dliness gradually and in measure — by rectifying the physical medameh so that complete emunah can be implanted even within it. This is the essential holiness of Tefillin received from the highest elder who encompasses all elders and all Mochin of Tefillin, and who rectifies everything.

Therefore the hide must be from a kosher animal or wild beast specifically — from a species permitted for consumption — even from neveilos and treifos of those species — as long as it is not from an impure species. Also, the hide must be processed lishmah [for the sake of the sanctity of Tefillin]. For one cannot receive the light of the holy Mochin of Tefillin unless the hide of the body is completely processed — with no grip and not even a whiff of any desire in the world remaining.

This is what our awesome Rebbe expressed precisely in his holy conversations: one must process the body like a hide that is processed well, until it can be turned over and seen with the eyes to be completely clean. He also said: there are great people who have broken bodily desires, but the body is still like processed hide that retains some bad odor. Rather, one must refine and process the body until not even a trace of any desire remains.

This is the refinement of the body — the processing of the hide (= the medameh, Nogah — the source of all desires). Through this they merit complete Mochin and complete emunah in ultimate perfection. Fortunate are they! But the common people who do not merit to refine the body to this degree — even complete Tzaddikim do not all merit such refinement — their essential tikun is through closeness to true Tzaddikim who, through their own bodily refinement, merited great true Mochin, Ruach Nevuah, and true Ruach HaKodesh. Through this, they can purify the medameh of the entire world so that all can merit complete emunah.

But there must be at least some is'arusa dil'sata [arousal from below]. Without it, it is impossible to extract them from where they are against their will. The essential is'arusa dil'sata is: strip away one's own opinion, remove one's wisdom and intellect entirely as if one has no intellect at all — only incline the ear and heart well to the voice of the true Tzaddik and surrender one's heart and intellect to him completely. As our Rebbe said: as long as a person retains any of his own intellect, he is not truly close at all. As explained on the verse "Am naval v'lo chacham" — "A nation that received the Torah and were not wise" (LM I:123): the essential receiving of the Torah was only through this — by removing their wisdom entirely. Had they stood on their own wisdom and intellect, they could not have received the Torah.

For the intellect of the entire world — even of the G-d-fearing and upright — as long as they have not broken their heart's desires completely, utterly, like truly processed hide without even a trace of odor — they still have no real intellect at all, and all their intellect is only in the aspect of the medameh, the animalistic, bodily power. Since they have not yet completely stripped their body of its animality, and their medameh is not yet fully purified — their essential tikun to draw close to Hashem is through emunas Chachamim: "Vaya'aminu BaHashem uv'Moshe avdo" — "They believed in Hashem and in Moshe His servant" (Shemos 14:31). To draw close to true Tzaddikim, believe in them, and nullify one's opinion before them entirely, as if one has no intellect at all.

This is the aspect of the halachah that STA"M may be written even on the hide of a neveilah and treifah — as long as it is from a kosher species.
